key_insight: Physics can be embedded directly as a neural network, yielding a training-free emulator that preserves the numerical scheme while matching solver accuracy.
engineering_relevance: PolyNet offers a fast, hardware-friendly alternative for simulating PDEs with strong GPU throughput and scalable ensemble execution, without retraining for known dynamics.
method: Continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics
Simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration
Coefficients are fixed from the governing physics, so no training is required
evidence_signal: On the 1D KdV equation, the authors compare PolyNet against CPU/GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural baselines over grid resolutions, 10^6 time steps, and ensembles up to 10^4 trajectories, using analytic soliton solutions to measure amplitude and phase error.
watch_item: The approach depends on having known governing coefficients and a suitable polynomial-form dynamics model, so applicability may be limited when physics is incomplete or strongly non-polynomial.
paper_title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation
